_note: Provisional picks (2026-10-13): transcription-checked, accent not yet judged by a human. Qwen3-TTS CustomVoice via VoiceStudio; never send 'language'. 2026-10-14: this engine IGNORES the 'instructions' text (same seed + other instructions = byte-identical audio; studio/voice_take.py probes this once per voice/model and caches the answer in work/_voice_probe.json). The field is kept for other engines but nothing relies on it. The pitch register comes from the SEED, so the whole script is voiced in ONE request and a take that is not steady is re-rolled with the next seed. ref_f0_hz = median pitch of the sample the user listened to (ref_sample, measured with 'python3 studio/voice_take.py refs'); every take must land within max_ref_st semitones of it (default 4.0). 2026-10-14 (German): 'de' is voiced by its OWN engine, Thorsten-Voice/Kokoro (Apache-2.0, dataset CC0), a small server in voice-de/ (start it with voice-de/run.sh start). engine_url = where the speech request goes; transcription (the per-line voice check) stays on VoiceStudio. deterministic = the same text gives the same audio, so the pipeline makes ONE take and never re-rolls seeds or patches lines: a line that fails the voice check has to be reworded. The Aiden voice (Qwen3, English-native) failed whole scripts (24 seeds: de-funkuhr, de-noise-cancelling). 2026-10-15: finished English videos sat at 167-238 Hz (the seed picks the register), so 'en' sets max_ref_st = 2.0, the most semitones a take may be from ref_f0_hz; a language without max_ref_st keeps the default 4.0 of studio/voice_take.py (German has ONE take and cannot be re-rolled). 2026-10-15 (English): 'en' now has its OWN engine too, Kokoro af_heart (US female, Apache-2.0), a small server in voice-en/ (start it with voice-en/run.sh start; 'start_hint' is the text the preflight shows when the engine is not running, default voice-<language>/run.sh start), because the Qwen3 voice Ryan changed its pitch with every seed, so finished English videos sounded like different people. Kokoro says the same text the same way every time, so English now follows the one-take rule of German above (a failing line is reworded); the sentences above about seeds and instructions describe the old Qwen voices only.
